source.title: A local-global principle for twisted flag varieties
readSections: Entire author manuscript dated 26 December 2025: introduction, §§1–5, appendices §§6–7, references; 26 body pages plus HAL cover
Compared older arXiv 2301.07572v3 (24 March 2023), 19 pages; it is not the extraction base
Gille errata dated 26 May 2026, entry for this paper, p. 1; GPS2021 entry pp. 1–2
Gille 2024, Loop group schemes and Abhyankar’s lemma: pp. 159–165, §§1–4.3, especially published Lemma 3 and Theorems 4,6
GPS2021 HAL v6, §§3.1–3.4, pp. 5–7: U_last and Lie-span inputs
Chernousov–Gille–Reichstein author manuscript, Theorem 1.2(b), §§4–5: integral finite subgroup, normalizer and toral reduction
Gille–Stavrova arXiv manuscript, Proposition 7.7, pp. 40–41: henselian invariance, applied with the identity simply connected cover
source.versionNote: Locators without a prefix are the 26-page HAL author manuscript. The publisher landing page verifies publication metadata, not the inaccessible article text. The URL ending .pdf returned a PDF rendering of the paywall page, not the article. Known numbering comparison: HAL Example 4.1(b)/Proposition 5.2 correspond to errata published Example 5.1(b)/Proposition 6.2; HAL main Theorem 5.4 corresponds to publisher Theorem 6.4. Do not blindly shift other locators.

summary: Extracts the complete author text and its analytic, semilocal, patching and tame-loop proof chain. The main divisorial theorem assumes residue characteristic exponent prime to the absolute-root-system automorphism order; all-rank-one local-global and finite-patch results are unconditional. Imports existing Banach submersion, analytic differentiation, simply connected field-group and DVR-model declarations. Partial checkpoint: G1 literal derivative hypothesis, G2 optional closure theorem prerequisites, G3 Tits-index directions versus final published text, G4 full scope of affine-quotient surface purity remain explicitly quarantined. Corrected mathematical statements are distinguished from quotations.

items.name: Semiglobal field and characteristic exponent
items.statement: T is a complete discrete valuation ring, K=Frac(T), k its residue field; p=1 if char(k)=0, otherwise p=char(k). X/K is a smooth projective geometrically integral curve and F=K(X).
items.note: API: Store T,K,k,X,F, uniformizer and embeddings; separate residue characteristic from field characteristic. Tests: (1) K(x) from P1_K satisfies the definition; (2) char(k)=0 gives p=1, never a prime 0; (3) k may be infinite or imperfect; no local compactness follows.

items.name: Reductive group scheme
items.statement: A reductive S-group is a smooth affine group scheme with geometrically connected reductive fibres. Relative reductivity is fibrewise, not linear reductivity.
items.note: API: Base change, fibres, adjoint quotient and passage to field groups. Tests: (1) G_m over Z is reductive; (2) G_a over a field is not reductive; (3) SL2 in positive characteristic is reductive without semisimple rational representation category.

items.name: Simply connected semisimple field group
items.statement: A semisimple affine group over a field is simply connected if every central isogeny from a semisimple group onto it is an isomorphism; in coordinate Hopf algebras the arrow reverses.
items.note: Read SimplyConnected/Basic.lean:67–80 at f790474. This does not supply the relative-base simply connected theory. API: Use the existing Hopf-coordinate object property; transport by the group/Hopf dictionary. Tests: (1) Coordinate central-isogeny arrow goes out of H; (2) Only semisimple sources are quantified; (3) An isomorphism satisfies the universal property; arbitrary finite covers are not the predicate.

items.name: Parabolic type convention
items.statement: Choose a Borel/maximal-torus pair over F_s with simple roots Delta. Standard parabolics P_I are indexed increasingly by I subset Delta: P_empty=B, P_Delta=G. Rational types are stable under the star action.
items.note: API: Type, inclusion, transport under conjugacy and Galois action. Tests: (1) Empty type gives a Borel; (2) Full type gives G; (3) Increasing I enlarges the parabolic, not its flag dimension.

items.name: Anisotropic subset of the Tits index
items.statement: Delta_0(G) is the type of a minimal F-parabolic, using the increasing convention. For a star-stable I, Par_I(G)(F) is nonempty exactly when Delta_0(G) is contained in I.
items.note: API: Transport Delta_0 in a common absolute diagram; base-change inclusion; admissible-type criterion. Tests: (1) Split semisimple G has Delta_0 empty; (2) An anisotropic nontrivial semisimple G has Delta_0=Delta; (3) A torus has empty absolute diagram and its flag is a point.

items.name: Twisted flag variety with its group action
items.statement: A twisted flag of reductive G/F is an integral G-variety whose base change to F_s is G_Fs/P_I for a smooth parabolic P_I. Its type I is star-stable and it is canonically the scheme Par_I(G).
items.note: API: Retain the action and type, rational-point/parabolic equivalence, base change and adjoint/SC comparison. Tests: (1) Type Delta gives Spec(F); (2) Split SL_n line flags give projective space; (3) A quotient by a non-smooth subgroup in characteristic p is not accepted merely because it is projective.

items.name: Representability and smooth properness of parabolic schemes
items.statement: For a reductive group scheme, the parabolic functor is represented by a smooth projective scheme, with components indexed by locally constant types; a permissible fixed-type component represents parabolics of that type.
items.note: General representability and non-split type descent extend the dynamic cocharacter point-subgroups already present in Tau Ceti.

items.name: Dual conventions for vector schemes
items.statement: For a quasi-coherent module E, V(E)=Spec Sym(E) represents linear maps from pulled-back E to O. For finite locally free E, W(E)=V(E dual) represents sections of E.
items.note: API: Duality identification, addition/scalar multiplication and base change. Tests: (1) For E=O^n both give affine n-space with the specified coordinate dual; (2) W(E)(Y)=Gamma(Y,E_Y); (3) Double dual identification requires finite local freeness.

items.name: R-equivalence over a ring
items.statement: For a ring B set Sigma={f in B[t] : f(0),f(1) are units}. Direct R-equivalence in X(B) uses a point of X(B[t]_Sigma) with the prescribed endpoints; R-equivalence is the equivalence relation it generates.
items.note: API: Endpoint evaluation maps, path reversal/composition at the generated-relation level, functoriality. Tests: (1) A polynomial path gives direct equivalence when defined at both endpoints; (2) For G_m, the segment from 1 to u uses endpoint-unit localization, not a unit in B[t]; (3) Do not identify this with direct R1-equivalence from the different errata entry.

items.name: Normal subgroup of R-trivial points
items.statement: For a B-group scheme G, points R-equivalent to 1 form a normal subgroup RG(B); G(B)/R is a group and base-change homomorphisms descend to it.
items.note: Use products, inverse and conjugation of rational paths; no commutativity assumption.

items.name: Proper and strictly proper parabolics
items.statement: A parabolic over S is everywhere proper if each fibre is proper; it is strictly proper if its image in every absolute adjoint simple factor of every geometric fibre is proper. A reductive group is strictly isotropic if it has such a parabolic.
items.note: API: Base change and locality, factorwise test, distinction from ordinary properness. Tests: (1) B×G in G×G is proper but not strictly proper; (2) A Borel in a split semisimple group is strictly proper; (3) The trivial-root torus case is interpreted factorwise, not by forcing a proper subgroup.

items.name: Automorphism and diagram torsors
items.statement: For adjoint G of constant type over connected normal integral S, a Chevalley form G0 has smooth Aut(G0), exact sequence 1→G0→Aut(G0)→Aut(Delta0)→1, and Isom(G0,G) is its torsor; the diagram quotient is finite etale.
items.note: API: Twist G0, form the diagram torsor and its monodromy; stabilizer subgroups Aut_I. Tests: (1) The split group gives the trivial torsor; (2) An inner twist has trivial diagram action; (3) Aut_I contains inner automorphisms and only diagram automorphisms fixing I.

items.name: Generic fundamental group surjection for normal bases
items.statement: For connected normal integral S with function field F and compatible geometric points, Gamma_F→pi_1(S) is surjective; a subset of the diagram invariant under Gamma_F is invariant under pi_1(S).

items.name: Reduction of the form torsor to the type stabilizer
items.statement: A monodromy-stable subset I of the Chevalley diagram gives a section of Q/Aut_I(G0)=D/Aut_I(Delta0), hence an Aut_I(G0)-reduction Q_I; twist Par_I(G0) by Q_I.
items.note: API: Reduction/section correspondence, associated flag bundle and restriction to the generic fibre. Tests: (1) I=Delta gives the point flag; (2) I empty gives the Borel scheme with the whole diagram stabilizer; (3) A non-invariant I cannot be descended as a fixed-type component.

items.name: Extension of a twisted flag along a reductive model
items.statement: If S is normal integral and G extends to a reductive S-group, every twisted flag of G_F extends to a smooth projective S-scheme of the same permissible type.
items.note: Reduce to the adjoint group of constant type; use the diagram-torsor construction, not an arbitrary projective compactification.

items.name: Elementary subgroup attached to an opposite pair
items.statement: For a semilocal A and strictly isotropic reductive H/A, choose a strictly proper P and opposite P−. H(A)^+ is generated by Ru(P)(A) and Ru(P−)(A).
items.note: API: Canonical subgroup after independence proof, maps under base change and central isogenies. Tests: (1) For split SL2 over a field this is generated by upper/lower elementary matrices; (2) For a product take both simple factors; (3) No subgroup H(A)^+ is introduced through a nonexistent strictly proper P.

items.name: Independence and normality of the elementary subgroup
items.statement: For a semilocal ring and strictly isotropic reductive group, the elementary subgroup is independent of strictly proper P and opposite P− and is normal in H(A).

items.name: Semilocal elementary-parabolic decomposition
items.statement: For semilocal A, H/A strictly isotropic and P strictly proper, H(A)=H(A)^+ P(A).
items.note: Uses the semilocal U U− P decomposition; do not require a field or semilocal residue perfection.

items.name: Henselian invariance of the elementary quotient
items.statement: If (A,I) is a henselian pair with A semilocal and I contained in its Jacobson radical, and H/A is semisimple simply connected strictly isotropic, reduction induces H(A)/H(A)^+ ≅ H(A/I)/H(A/I)^+.
items.note: Read Gille–Stavrova Proposition 7.7 directly. Their more general statement assumes the simply connected covering morphism smooth; for the simply connected H used here that morphism is the identity. No prime-to-characteristic hypothesis is needed in this specialization.

items.name: Finite algebra as a product of local Artin algebras
items.statement: A nonzero finite-dimensional commutative k-algebra A is a finite product of Artin local A_i with residue fields k_i; A_i may be nonreduced and k_i/k inseparable.
items.note: Reuse the pinned Artinian quotient decomposition and nilradical nilpotence in items 127–128. The missing portion is the finite-local-factor/residue-field packaging with coherent maps for the torsor argument, not the commutative algebra theorem. API: Local factors, maximal ideals, residue maps and nilpotence filtration. Tests: (1) k[epsilon]/epsilon² is one nonreduced factor; (2) k×k has two factors; (3) A finite purely inseparable field is allowed.

items.name: Affine Weil restriction
items.statement: For finite locally free A/k and affine finitely presented A-scheme H, Res_A/k H represents B↦H(A tensor_k B), compatibly with base change, products and composition.
items.note: API: Adjunction and algebra-valued points; group laws when H is a group. Tests: (1) Res_A/k affine n-space has dimension n dim_k A; (2) Res along k×k is a product; (3) Finite inseparable restriction of a reductive group is not automatically reductive.

items.name: Smooth connected restriction over finite algebras
items.statement: If A is a nonzero finite k-algebra and H is reductive over A, Res_A/k H is a smooth connected affine k-group. It need not be reductive.
items.note: Requires the nilpotent-algebra and inseparable Weil-restriction smoothness/connectedness results, beyond the separable reductivity clause of RG2.0a.

items.name: R-equivalence and restriction of scalars
items.statement: In the preceding finite-algebra setting, the point identity (Res_A/k H)(k)=H(A) induces an isomorphism of R-equivalence quotients.
items.note: Supply the comparison of endpoint-unit localizations; a bare point bijection is not sufficient.

items.name: R-equivalence insensitive to the Artin nilpotents
items.statement: For the same A=product A_i and H, H(A)/R ≅ product_i H(k_i)/R.

items.name: Square-zero devissage of finite local algebras
items.statement: For local Artin A with maximal ideal m and m^(n+1)=0, use A_j=A/m^(j+1), j=0,…,n. The kernel A_j→A_(j−1) is m^j/m^(j+1), square-zero for j≥1.
items.note: API: Finite tower and Lie-valued congruence kernels of smooth groups. Tests: (1) A=k[epsilon]/epsilon³ has two nontrivial steps; (2) At j=2 the kernel is m²/m³, not mA_j; (3) The tower ends at A_n=A, not A_(n−1).

items.name: Vector-kernel torsors preserve R-classes in the nilpotent tower
items.statement: In the finite-Artin smooth-group tower the Weil-restricted kernel is a vector group Lie(H) tensor the square-zero ideal; its torsor over the affine previous stage is trivial, giving a scheme product and an isomorphism on R-classes.
items.note: Use vanishing of H1 of quasi-coherent additive sheaves on affine schemes, not the false assertion that every unipotent torsor is trivial.

items.name: Elementary subgroup equals R-trivial subgroup over fields
items.statement: For a semisimple simply connected strictly isotropic group over a field, H(k)^+=RH(k).
items.note: This is not the assertion H(k)^+=H(k); Kneser–Tits vanishing is stronger.

items.name: Elementary subgroup equals R-trivial subgroup over finite algebras
items.statement: For semisimple simply connected strictly isotropic H over a finite nonzero k-algebra A, H(A)^+=RH(A); reduction and restriction of scalars identify the elementary and R-equivalence quotients with the product over residue fields.
items.note: Use henselian invariance and the preceding field theorem, retaining semisimplicity.

items.name: Weil topology on points over a valued field
items.statement: For a nontrivially valued field L, give X(L) for a finite-type L-scheme its chart topology; regular morphisms are continuous and product/open/closed immersion comparisons hold.
items.note: Generalize the basic topology part of RG2.0; leave its compactness conclusions under finite-residue local-field hypotheses. API: Chart independence, rational-point functor and group topology. Tests: (1) Affine n-space has the finite product topology; (2) An open subscheme gives an open subset; (3) Infinite residue fields do not imply local compactness.

items.name: Complete module data for local analytic factorization
items.statement: T⊂R0 are complete DVRs with common uniformizer t, K=Frac(T), F0=Frac(R0), |t|=alpha^(-1), alpha>1. F1,F2⊂F0 contain K. T-submodules V⊂F1∩R0 and W⊂F2∩R0 are t-adically complete, V+W=R0 and V∩tR0=tV, W∩tR0=tW.
items.note: API: Saturated modules, embeddings into F0 and localized K-Banach spaces. Tests: (1) V=R0,W=0 meets the hypotheses; (2) Saturation at t implies the corresponding identities at all t powers; (3) The common uniformizer condition cannot be inferred from an arbitrary ramified DVR inclusion.

items.name: Closedness of the complete saturated module
items.statement: Under the module data V is closed in R0, and likewise W.

items.name: Norm on localized module elements
items.statement: If v=u/t^n with u in V but not tV, then |v|=alpha^n; zero is handled separately.

items.name: Module as the integral ball in its localization
items.statement: V={v in V[1/t]: |v|≤1}; this is open and closed in V[1/t].
items.note: The author text prints |v|≥0, which is all of V[1/t]. The integral-ball inequality is ≤1.

items.name: Localized modules are Banach subspaces
items.statement: V[1/t] and W[1/t] are closed K-vector subspaces of F0 and hence complete for the restricted norm.
items.note: These spaces need not be finite-dimensional over K.

items.name: Analytic functions have a strict derivative
items.statement: For normed spaces over a nontrivially normed field, an analytic function at x has strict derivative fderiv at x; in this application all spaces are complete.
items.note: Read Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Analytic.lean:141–145 at 082e2d3; apply with the complete spaces here, and restrict scalars and precompose with closed-subspace inclusions.

items.name: Strict submersion maps a neighbourhood filter onto a neighbourhood filter
items.statement: For complete normed spaces E,F over a nontrivially normed field, if f has strict derivative f′ at a and range(f′)=top, then map f (nhds a)=nhds(f(a)).
items.note: Read Analysis/Calculus/InverseFunctionTheorem/FDeriv.lean:76–98. No complemented kernel or finite-dimensional K-space hypothesis is required.

items.name: Unresolved literal derivative hypothesis in Proposition 3.3
items.statement: The printed hypothesis uses Df_v(V[1/t]^a)+Df_w(V[1/t]^b)=F0^c while the desired image restricts the second variable to W^b. Taken literally this implication is false.
items.note: G1. Counterexample: V=R0,W=0,a=b=c=1,f(v,w)=w. The printed derivative sum is F0 but f(V×W)={0}. Confirm the final published wording; keep this literal assertion out of routes. The corrected mathematical result is the next item.

items.name: Corrected local analytic surjectivity
items.statement: For the module data, let f be analytic on an open neighbourhood of (0,0) in F0^a×F0^b, f(0,0)=0, a,b,c>0. If Df_v(V[1/t]^a)+Df_w(W[1/t]^b)=F0^c, some epsilon>0 has every y with |y|≤epsilon in f((V^a×W^b)∩domain(f)).
items.note: Apply the library strict submersion theorem to the restricted K-Banach domain. The second module must be W; the manuscript also mis-types one derivative domain. This item is a proved correction proposed for review, not a silent quotation.

items.name: Analytic multiplication-type factorization near zero
items.statement: For equal input/output dimension n and analytic f with f(x,0)=f(0,x)=x near zero, the module hypotheses imply that all sufficiently small y are f(v,w) with v in V^n and w in W^n.
items.note: Both partial derivatives are identity, so the corrected derivative condition follows from V+W=R0.

items.name: Field data for group factorization
items.statement: Add to the module data a common subfield F⊂F1∩F2, a finite field extension E/F, and density of F1 in F0. The extension E/F need not be separable. Put G=Res_E/F H for reductive H/E.
items.note: API: Artin-algebra points H(E tensor Fi), plus/R subgroups and compatible embeddings. Tests: (1) E tensor Fi can be nonreduced; (2) F1 density is added here, not in Proposition 3.3; (3) G may be nonreductive even when H is semisimple.

items.name: Product-compatible last unipotent subgroup
items.statement: For a strictly proper parabolic P of a reductive group, take in each absolute adjoint simple factor the last term of Demazure’s filtration of Ru(P), then descend their product. The resulting U_last is a central vector subgroup of Ru(P), equivariant under Aut(G,P).
items.note: API: Base change, vector coordinates and factorwise definition independent of decomposition. Tests: (1) For split SL2 this is the positive root group; (2) For factors with different filtration lengths take the last term in each factor; (3) A global last nonzero term alone can omit a simple factor.

items.name: Conjugates of the last unipotent Lie algebra span
items.statement: Over an infinite field E, for H semisimple simply connected and P strictly proper, the E-span of Ad(H(E)^+)Lie(U_last) is Lie(H).
items.note: GPS pp. 5–7 read directly. E is infinite here because it contains K, the fraction field of a DVR; no characteristic restriction is introduced.

items.name: Etale coordinates with values in the elementary subgroup
items.statement: Choose finitely many h_i in H(E)^+ whose conjugated Lie(U_last) span Lie(H). The product of conjugate unipotent elements has surjective derivative at zero; restrict to a linear complement to get an etale chart at identity. Restrict scalars to F and use the complete-field analytic inverse theorem.
items.note: API: Chart, derivative, coordinate neighbourhood and elementary image. Tests: (1) Every factor is h_i u_i h_i^(-1), so zero maps to 1; (2) The complement is finite-dimensional over E at this step; (3) Weil restriction of an etale chart works for finite inseparable E/F too.

items.name: Elementary subgroup is open in the ambient group
items.statement: Under the group-factorization data with H/E semisimple strictly isotropic, G(F0)^+ is open in G(F0).
items.note: The printed phrase open subgroup of G(F0)^+ is tautological; the constructed chart proves openness in G(F0).

items.name: Elementary factorization over the diamond
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, G(F0)^+=G(F1)^+G(F2)^+.

items.name: Central covers induce surjections on elementary subgroups
items.statement: For a semisimple group H and its simply connected central cover Hsc, each corresponding parabolic unipotent radical is carried isomorphically to the other, so Hsc(B)^+→H(B)^+ is onto for the finite Artin algebras B used here.
items.note: Use Res(Hsc)→Res(H), not a simply connected cover of a possibly nonreductive Res(H).

items.name: Quasi-trivial torus covering a maximal torus
items.statement: For a maximal E-torus T of reductive H, choose a smooth surjection of E-tori Q→T with Q quasi-trivial and torus kernel. Q is an open subset of affine space via products of restrictions of G_m.
items.note: API: Character-lattice construction, smooth differential and rational parametrization near 1. Tests: (1) A split torus can use its identity cover; (2) A surjective isogeny with non-smooth kernel is not a replacement; (3) The open-affine parametrization supplies R-trivial paths.

items.name: Conjugated maximal-torus Lie algebras span
items.statement: For reductive H over the infinite field E, finitely many conjugates of Lie(T) for a maximal torus T span Lie(H), and the corresponding conjugate product from Q factors has surjective derivative.
items.note: This is a distinct input from the simply connected unipotent spanning theorem.

items.name: R-trivial subgroup is open
items.statement: Under the group-factorization data with H reductive, RG(F0) is an open subgroup of G(F0).

items.name: Two R-trivial patch subgroups contain a neighbourhood
items.statement: Under the same data, RG(F1)RG(F2) contains an identity neighbourhood in G(F0).

items.name: R-factorization under density of R-points
items.statement: If moreover RG(F1) is dense in RG(F0), then RG(F0)=RG(F1)RG(F2).
items.note: Do not assume the product is a subgroup. For A=RG(F1), B=RG(F2), N⊂AB an identity neighbourhood and g∈RG(F0), choose a∈A∩gN^(-1); then g∈aN⊂AB.

items.name: One isotropic patch gives mixed elementary/R factorization
items.statement: If H is semisimple simply connected and H_(E tensor F1) is strictly isotropic, then G(F0)^+=G(F1)^+ RG(F2).
items.note: The strict-isotropy hypothesis is on the F1 Artin algebra; it cannot be replaced just by isotropy over F0.

items.name: Two isotropic patches give elementary factorization
items.statement: If H is semisimple simply connected and both H_(E tensor Fi), i=1,2, are strictly isotropic, then G(F0)^+=G(F1)^+G(F2)^+.

items.name: Closure of the first R-subgroup is open
items.statement: Under the group-factorization data, closure(RG(F1)) is an open subgroup of G(F0).
items.note: The overline is essential. It is present in the page image, though plain text can lose it.

items.name: Optional closure factorization theorem
items.statement: If E/F is separable, H/E semisimple simply connected, and G_F0 strictly isotropic, then closure(RG(F1))=RG(F1)RG(F2)=G(F0)^+.
items.note: G2. Statement read from page image. Before routing, verify the exact hypotheses of Kaletha–Prasad Proposition 2.14, Harder torus approximation and Tits normal-subgroup input for arbitrary residue fields. This optional result is not used in Theorem 3.13. The final density step should use Proposition 3.9(2); (3) demands an unproved F1-isotropy assumption.

items.name: Unbounded projections of the closure subgroup
items.statement: In Proposition 3.11(2), closure(RG(F1)) projects unboundedly to every F0-almost-simple factor.
items.note: G2 dependency. The torus argument needs (Tsharp(F1))^n⊂RTsharp(F1), not all Tsharp(F1)⊂RTsharp(F1). Exact Harder/Prasad scope remains unverified.

items.name: Open subdirect product repair in the optional theorem
items.statement: For H open in a finite product of the relevant elementary simple-factor groups, if each projection is onto, H∩G_i is open and normal in G_i. If every proper normal subgroup of G_i is central and an open subgroup cannot be central, then H is the whole product.
items.note: Surjective projections alone do not make H normal: a diagonal subgroup of S3×S3 is a counterexample. Use the factor intersections, openness and the explicitly supplied normal-subgroup theorem. This abstract repair does not discharge G2.

items.name: Weil restriction of a projective flag
items.statement: For finite E/F and a twisted flag X/E, construct Z=Res_E/F X as a scheme, with Z(L)=X(E tensor_F L), including inseparable extensions.
items.note: RG2.0a owns affine restriction; it does not by itself represent this nonaffine functor. API: Nonaffine representability, base change, point adjunction, composition. Tests: (1) For separable E/F the splitting-base-change scheme is a product of flags; (2) For inseparable E/F a projective source does not imply its restriction is proper; (3) Point adjunction holds over nonreduced E tensor L.

items.name: Semilocal transitivity on same-type parabolics
items.statement: For reductive H over a semilocal ring A, two parabolics of the same type are H(A)-conjugate. If H is strictly isotropic, the decomposition H(A)=H(A)^+P(A) gives elementary transitivity on the corresponding pointed flag.

items.name: Reduction to absolutely simple groups and flag products
items.statement: A semisimple simply connected group over E decomposes into products of restrictions of absolutely almost simple groups over finite separable extensions of E; its twisted flags decompose into the corresponding products and restrictions.
items.note: The extensions over E are separable; their composites with an originally inseparable E/F may remain inseparable over F.

items.name: Descent of an equal pair of field-valued points
items.statement: If F1,F2⊂F0 have intersection F and a separated finite-type F-scheme Z has points z_i∈Z(F_i) with the same F0-image, they descend to a unique F-point.
items.note: Choose an F-affine open containing the common image; its coordinate values lie in F1∩F2. The maps on underlying points and affine-open factorization must be checked.

items.name: Flag local-global principle for the analytic diamond
items.statement: Under the module and group data, additionally F=F1∩F2, for any reductive H/E and twisted flag X/E, Z=Res_E/F X satisfies Z(F)≠empty iff Z(F1) and Z(F2) are nonempty.
items.note: For x1=h x2 and h=h1h2, glue h1^(-1)x1=h2 x2. The manuscript prints an incorrect inverse on h2. No rationality of H and no separability of E/F are assumed.

items.name: Existing DVR model carrier
items.statement: A flat finitely presented model over DVR T records its total scheme, map to Spec T and chosen identification of its generic fibre with X/K; properness is a separate predicate.
items.note: Read Curves/StableReduction/Model/Basic.lean:43–73 at f790474. API: Use Model and its morphisms; add normality/projectivity separately. Tests: (1) The generic-fibre identification is data; (2) Properness is not in the bare carrier; (3) No normality or curve dimension is supplied by Model alone.

items.name: Normal projective curve model
items.statement: A model mathcal X/T here is connected normal integral flat projective of relative dimension one, with generic fibre the prescribed smooth geometrically integral X/K; denote its closed fibre Y.
items.note: API: Generic/special fibres, proper birational refinements and codimension-one valuations. Tests: (1) P1_T is a model of K(x); (2) Special fibre need not be irreducible or reduced; (3) Normal model is stronger than the existing bare Model carrier.

items.name: Completed local patch field
items.statement: For P∈Y set R_P=O_(mathcal X),P, Rhat_P its completion at the maximal ideal, and F_P=Frac(Rhat_P). For a closed point this is the full maximal-ideal completion, not merely the t-adic one.
items.note: API: Embeddings F→F_P, complete local ring and comparison with branches. Tests: (1) At infinity of P1_T, Rhat_P=T[[x^(-1)]]; (2) Closed-point completion uses (t,x^(-1)); (3) A generic point of Y has a DVR completion.

items.name: Completed open patch field
items.statement: For nonempty affine U in one component of Y, disjoint from the other components, R_U is the subring of F regular at every point of U, Rhat_U its t-adic completion, and F_U=Frac(Rhat_U).
items.note: API: Restriction under shrinking U, normality/excellence and field embeddings. Tests: (1) For P1 over k[[t]] and U=A1_k, Rhat_U=k[x][[t]]; (2) Frac(k[x][[t]]) embeds properly in k(x)((t)); (3) Completion and fraction-field formation cannot be exchanged.

items.name: Branch field and valuation ring
items.statement: A branch at closed P is a height-one prime of Rhat_P containing t. Localize there and complete to a complete DVR Rhat_branch; its fraction field F_branch receives F_P and F_U for the associated component U.
items.note: API: Incidence relation, localization/completion embeddings and normalization of valuation. Tests: (1) A node can have two branches; (2) t need not be a branch uniformizer for a nonreduced fibre; (3) For the P1 infinity branch over k[[t]], F_branch=k((x^(-1)))((t)).

items.name: Finite patching system
items.statement: Choose a finite nonempty set P of closed points of Y containing all intersections of irreducible components, and with affine connected components U of Y minus P. Let B be the branches linking P and U; retain all field inclusions.
items.note: API: Incidence graph, products of point/open/branch fields, refinement. Tests: (1) On P1 use P={infinity}, U={A1}; (2) Include every component intersection; (3) Do not replace the inverse-limit diagram by a single product field.

items.name: The projective-line patching diamond
items.statement: For mathcal X=P1_T, P=infinity and U=A1_k, take F=K(x), F1=F_P,F2=F_U,F0=F_branch,V=Rhat_P,W=Rhat_U inside R0=Rhat_branch.
items.note: API: Explicit ring embeddings, common t-uniformizer and patch intersection. Tests: (1) V=T[[x^(-1)]]; (2) W is the t-adic completion of S^(-1)T[x] for S unit modulo t; (3) Do not replace V,W by the generally larger F_i∩R0.

items.name: Projective-line modules satisfy the analytic hypotheses
items.statement: For the preceding P1 diamond, V and W are t-complete and saturated, V+W=R0, and F1 is dense in F0.
items.note: The polynomial approximation for W uses T[x], not T[x^(-1)]. Prove density of the integral part in R0 and then invert t; a bounded integral subset is not dense in all of F0.

items.name: Coefficientwise Laurent splitting in equal characteristic
items.statement: When T=k[[t]], split each coefficient in k((x^(-1))) into its positive powers of x and its nonpositive powers. The nonpositive-x-power part lies in V=k[[x^(-1),t]], the positive polynomial part in W=k[x][[t]].
items.note: The printed assignment of f1,f2 to V,W is reversed. API: Additive decomposition with a chosen allocation of the constant term. Tests: (1) x belongs to W; (2) x^(-1) belongs to V; (3) The coefficient field assumption is needed for this explicit coefficientwise formula.

items.name: Correct fraction field of the completed open ring
items.statement: For any field k, Frac(k[x][[t]]) is a proper subfield of k(x)((t)). A valid element outside it is sum_(n≥1) t^n/x^(n!).
items.locator: Example 4.1(b); May 26 2026 errata Example 5.1(b), with repaired witness
items.note: For a quotient a/b with a,b∈k[x][[t]], divide out the common t-order so b0≠0. If m=ord_x(b0), the coefficient recurrence gives ord_x(c_n)≥−m(n+1). Factorial pole growth violates every such linear bound. The errata witness sum t^n/x^n equals t/(x−t), so it lies inside the fraction field.

items.name: Intersection in the projective-line diamond
items.statement: Inside F_branch for the projective-line system, F_P∩F_U=K(x).

items.name: Finite map of a normal curve model to the projective line
items.statement: For the admissible finite patch set, choose a finite T-morphism mathcal X→P1_T whose inverse image of infinity is the chosen point set. It induces finite F/K(x) and identifications of the base-changed point/open/branch fields with their finite products on mathcal X.
items.note: API: Chosen finite morphism, compatible tensor-product decompositions and restriction of scalars. Tests: (1) The P1 identity recovers the basic diamond; (2) Tensor products over K(x) can be products, not fields; (3) Separability is not required by the analytic flag theorem; do not infer reductivity of Res G without it.

items.name: Finite-patch local-global principle for twisted flags
items.statement: For the finite patching system on any normal projective T-model, reductive G/F and twisted flag Z/F, Z(F)≠empty iff Z(F_P)≠empty for every P in the chosen finite set and Z(F_U)≠empty for every open component U.
items.note: No residue-characteristic restriction and no rationality assumption on G.

items.name: Unresolved literal Tits-index inclusion directions
items.statement: With Delta_0 defined as the minimal-parabolic type, the printed smallest star-stable subset contained in all local Delta_0 and the displayed global-to-local inclusion in Theorem 4.5(2) have the wrong direction.
items.note: G3. The empty subset is always star-stable and contained in every local subset, so that literal smallest-subset characterization always returns empty, even for an anisotropic group. The corrected union formulation is extracted separately. Check the subscription final version before claiming the discrepancy remains in print.

items.name: Correct finite-patch Tits-index formula
items.statement: Transport local absolute diagrams into Delta. Delta_0(G) is the smallest Gamma_F-stable subset of Delta containing every local Delta_0(G_Fxi), for xi running over the point and open patches.
items.note: Global minimal-parabolic type contains every local minimal type. Conversely any stable I containing them gives local Par_I points, then a global point by (1), hence Delta_0(G)⊂I. For circled vertices the equivalent formula uses the largest stable subset of the intersection of local circled sets.

items.name: Spread a generic special-fibre point to an open patch
items.statement: A point of a finite-type F-variety over F_eta for a generic point eta of Y spreads to a point over F_U for some nonempty sufficiently small affine U in that component.
items.note: This is a completed-patch approximation theorem, not ordinary spreading out over an uncompleted scheme.

items.name: Local-global principle using all special-fibre points
items.statement: For any normal model and twisted flag Z of reductive G/F, Z(F)≠empty iff Z(F_P)≠empty for every point P∈Y, including generic points.

items.name: Correct all-points Tits-index formula
items.statement: Delta_0(G) is the Gamma_F-stable closure of the union of transported Delta_0(G_FP) over every point P of the special fibre.
items.note: Derive by admissible types from (1), with the same convention correction as Theorem 4.5(2).

items.name: Discrete-valued local-global principle for a reductive model
items.statement: If G extends to a reductive group over a normal projective T-model, a twisted flag Z has an F-point iff it has F_v-points for every discrete valuation v of F.
items.note: For the proper-specialization argument, first pass to a regular model with strict-normal-crossing fibre using the surface resolution input, and pull back G and its smooth projective flag model. This avoids treating a singular special-fibre component as if it were a regular curve.

items.name: Correct index formula in the reductive-model case
items.statement: Under the preceding model-extension hypothesis, Delta_0(G) is the Gamma_F-stable closure of the union of local minimal-parabolic types at all discrete completions F_v.

items.name: Rank-one local points give a model with all completed local points
items.statement: For a smooth F-variety, the all-rank-one-valuations local-point hypothesis gives a regular projective T-model on which every F_P has a point, in the form used by HHKP Theorem 2.5.
items.note: The exact auxiliary theorem requires its own extraction; retain rank-one valuations, not just discrete ones.

items.name: Unconditional rank-one local-global principle
items.statement: For any reductive G/F and twisted flag Z/F, Z(F)≠empty iff Z(F_v)≠empty for every rank-one valuation v of F.
items.note: No residue-characteristic restriction; rank-one valuations need not be discrete.

items.name: Correct rank-one Tits-index formula
items.statement: For arbitrary reductive G/F, Delta_0(G) is the Gamma_F-stable closure of the union of local minimal-parabolic types at all rank-one completions.

items.name: Divisorial valuations of a semiglobal field
items.statement: The divisorial valuations considered in the main theorem arise from codimension-one points on normal projective T-models of the curve. Distinguish all such valuations from all discrete valuations and all rank-one valuations.
items.note: API: Valuation from a divisor, completion, birational transport and vertical/horizontal distinction. Tests: (1) A special-fibre component gives a valuation nontrivial on K; (2) A horizontal closed point of X gives one trivial on K; (3) The main proof only needs the nontrivial-on-K subfamily.

items.name: Strict-normal-crossing divisor on a regular surface
items.statement: On a regular two-dimensional model, the support of D is locally the zero set of a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters; multiplicities in a divisor do not change the open complement.
items.note: API: Local parameters, complement, total transform and support under modification. Tests: (1) At a crossing use two parameters; (2) At a smooth branch use one and, if necessary for a loop theorem, enlarge by a second parameter; (3) An arbitrary regular sequence is not automatically a normal-crossing coordinate divisor.

items.name: Spread a generic torsor to an open subset
items.statement: For a flat affine finitely presented group scheme H on the model, an H_F-torsor descends to some open subset; together with the stated generic-curve extension it extends over the complement of a suitable divisor.

items.name: Purity for reductive torsors on a regular surface
items.statement: If X is a regular scheme of dimension two, U contains all codimension-one points and G/X is reductive, restriction gives a bijection H1_fppf(X,G)→H1_fppf(U,G).
items.note: Source cites Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc Theorem 6.13. No general-dimensional purity claim is made.

items.name: Purity with an affine linear quotient
items.statement: If X is regular of dimension two, U contains its codimension-one points and an affine G/X admits Zariski-locally closed embeddings into GL_n with affine representable quotient, the source asserts H1_fppf(X,G)≅H1_fppf(U,G).
items.note: G4. The text says this follows by inspection of CTS Theorem 6.13. Verify the original proof and any flatness/finiteness assumptions on G and its quotient before routing this full generality. The application in Lemma 5.1 uses H flat affine of finite presentation; record that narrower target separately.

items.name: Surface torsor purity in the finite-presentation application
items.statement: For a flat affine finitely presented group H over a regular surface, with the local closed GL_n embeddings and affine quotient of Lemma 5.1, extend a torsor uniquely across the omitted codimension-two points.
items.note: Design must verify the CTS proof under precisely these hypotheses; the broader printed formulation is quarantined as G4. The assertion is a source theorem target, not a library claim.

items.name: Embedded resolution on an excellent regular surface
items.statement: Given the divisor in Lemma 5.1 over an excellent DVR, a proper birational modification yields a regular surface with strict-normal-crossing support of its total transform.
items.locator: Lemma 5.1, Lipman Theorem and Remark C
items.note: Use the proved two-dimensional excellent setting, including positive characteristic; no general resolution conjecture is needed.

items.name: Extend the torsor away from an SNC divisor
items.statement: Under Lemma 5.1: T excellent DVR, mathcal X regular flat projective curve model, H flat affine finitely presented with the local linear-affine-quotient property, and the generic torsor extension away from D_K, there is a proper birational regular model mathcal X′ and SNC-support divisor D′ such that the torsor extends over mathcal X′ minus D′.
items.note: This section initially needs excellent, not complete, T. Return to completeness for the semiglobal main theorem.

items.name: Prime-to-p finite structure reduction
items.statement: For the adjoint Chevalley form and star-stable I, choose the finite Z-subgroup S0⊂Aut_I(G0) supplied by Chernousov–Gille–Reichstein, whose H1 over F surjects onto the relevant forms and whose order has prime divisors among those of Aut(the absolute root system).
items.note: CGR author manuscript Theorem 1.2(b), §4 supplies the integral normalizer subgroup; its normalizer-to-group H1 comparison is toral reduction (§5). API: Finite-flat integral subgroup, prime-to-p etaleness over T and reduction of Q_I. Tests: (1) Use N_Aut_I(G0)(T0)/T0 for the finite Weyl/diagram quotient; (2) Aut_I(G0)/T0 itself is generally not finite; (3) When p is prime to the root-system automorphism order, S0,T is finite etale.

items.name: Reduction of form torsors to a finite subgroup
items.statement: Under p prime to the order of Aut(the absolute root system of G_ad), the type-preserving form torsor of G reduces to the finite etale prime-to-p subgroup S0 over the base DVR as used in Proposition 5.2.
items.note: Directly read CGR author manuscript Theorem 1.2(b), §§4–5 (GP26 cites published Theorem 1.1(b)). The finite subgroup lies in the normalizer. Pass to H1 of Aut_I using a maximal torus in the twisted adjoint identity component over F. The integral subgroup construction and enlargement preserve the set of prime divisors of the Weyl/diagram order; do not quotient Aut_I itself by a nonnormal torus.

items.name: Complete the regular local ring before the loop argument
items.statement: At a closed point P of the regular SNC model use A=completion(O_(mathcal X),P). Then A is regular henselian local of dimension two and the parameters defining D remain parameters; work on Spec A[1/D].
items.note: API: Completed SNC chart, pullback torsor and fraction field F_P. Tests: (1) The original uncompleted local ring need not be henselian; (2) Completion is at the full maximal ideal; (3) If D has one component, enlarge the inverted divisor to two parameters when applying the full-parameter loop theorem.

items.name: Loop cocycle and loop torsor
items.statement: For henselian regular local A with a chosen SNC coordinate divisor and U=Spec A[1/D], tame Kummer covers B_n/U have group mu_n(B)^r semidirect Gal(B/A), n prime to the residue characteristic. A loop cocycle takes values in G(B), not all G(B_n); a loop torsor is a torsor class represented by one.
items.note: API: Continuous finite-level cocycles, arithmetic/geometric parts and image in H1(U,G). Tests: (1) A constant cocycle from the unramified cover is loop; (2) The geometric part descends to mu_n^r→the arithmetic twist of G; (3) An arbitrary torsor is not declared loop without a reduction theorem.

items.name: Tame covers are dominated by Kummer-unramified covers
items.statement: For regular henselian A and a divisor cut by coordinate parameters, a tame finite etale cover of U is dominated by a cover obtained from a finite etale A-algebra and prime-to-p roots of the parameters, by Abhyankar’s lemma.
items.note: Use the correctly inverted Kummer algebra on U. The phrase finite degree prime to p alone is not a sufficient criterion for tame Galois closure.

items.name: Prime-to-p finite-group torsors are loop torsors
items.statement: If S/A is finite etale of constant degree prime to p, every S-torsor over U is a loop torsor, and its image under S→H is a loop H-torsor.
items.locator: Gille 2024 Lemma 3(2),(3), cited as Lemma 2.3 in GP26
items.note: Read pp. 162–163. For tameness, first make S constant by an unramified cover; inertia then has image in a group of order prime to p. This supplies the needed justification beyond the printed connected-cover degree argument.

items.name: Loop reductive group scheme
items.statement: A reductive group on U is loop if its Isom torsor from a Chevalley form is a loop Aut(G0)-torsor. The star action and a stable type I define the twisted parabolic scheme.
items.note: API: Adjoint/SC transport, type-stabilizer reduction and twisted flag scheme. Tests: (1) The split group is loop; (2) Adjoint and SC forms of a loop group remain loop; (3) Only a star-stable I gives the descended fixed-type flag.

items.name: Grothendieck valuation of a regular local surface
items.statement: Blow up the closed point of a regular local ring A of dimension two. At the generic point of the exceptional P1_k take its DVR; the residue field is k(u), and the fraction-field valuation gives the completion used by the loop theorem.
items.note: API: Exceptional divisor, DVR valuation, parameter and residue-field identification. Tests: (1) For k[[s,t]], choose t as uniformizer and u=s/t in the residue field; (2) The residue field is k(u), not k; (3) The valuation is divisorial on a birational model.

items.name: Completion comparison for the local and completed local rings
items.statement: For the regular two-dimensional local ring R_P and A=its maximal-ideal completion, their Grothendieck-valuation completions of fraction fields agree under the natural embedding: they have the same uniformizer and residue field k(P)(u), and successive approximation is dense.
items.note: The equality is between complete valued fields. Merely sharing residue and uniformizer would not identify arbitrary noncomplete subfields.

items.name: Smooth proper fixed locus for a tame geometric loop action
items.statement: For a loop cocycle acting on a smooth proper A-scheme Z, twist by the arithmetic part and take the fixed locus of its finite prime-to-p diagonalizable geometric part. The resulting Y is smooth proper over A.
items.note: Use the linearly reductive/tame fixed-locus theorem; no wild fixed-locus smoothness is asserted.

items.name: Fixed-point criterion over the Grothendieck completion
items.statement: For henselian regular local A with full coordinate divisor, affine finitely presented G acting on smooth proper Z and a loop cocycle phi, the twisted Z has a point over the Grothendieck completion iff its arithmetic-twisted geometric fixed locus has a k-point iff the twisted Z has a U-point.
items.note: Proof specializes the proper point through the tame extension and successive Laurent coordinates, then uses smooth henselian lifting. Extra divisor coordinates may be inverted for the GP26 fraction-field application.

items.name: Parabolic criterion for loop reductive groups
items.statement: For a loop reductive U-group and a star-stable type I, a U-parabolic of type I exists iff the geometric loop action normalizes such a parabolic over the residue field of the arithmetic twist iff the group over the Grothendieck completion has such a parabolic.
items.locator: Gille 2024 Theorem 6 (cited as Theorem 4.1(iii)⇒(i) in GP26)
items.note: Directly read the published prerequisite pp. 164–165; its numbering differs from the cited preprint. This is the descent input, not ordinary henselian lifting alone.

items.name: Divisorial points yield a model with completed-local points
items.statement: Under the main prime-to-root-automorphism-order hypothesis, if a twisted flag has points at every divisorial completion, there exists a regular proper T-model on which it has an F_P-point for every special-fibre point P.
items.note: Use finite structure reduction, SNC spreading, the corrected completed local A, the common Grothendieck completion and the loop parabolic criterion. Generic points are already divisorial.

items.name: Divisorial local-global principle for twisted flags
items.statement: Let F=K(X) be semiglobal as specified and p the characteristic exponent of k. For reductive G/F assume p does not divide |Aut(Phi(G_ad,F_s))|. Every twisted flag Z of G satisfies Z(F)≠empty iff Z(F_v)≠empty for every discrete valuation arising from codimension-one points of normal projective T-models.
items.note: Combines Proposition 5.2 with Corollary 4.6. The residue field is arbitrary; do not add finiteness/perfection or rationality of G.

items.name: Only valuations nontrivial on the constant field are needed
items.statement: In the main divisorial theorem, it suffices to test divisorial valuations v whose restriction to K is nontrivial.
items.note: This is a restriction of the tested family, not an extra hypothesis on every discrete valuation of F.

items.name: Replacement of the root-system order hypothesis by finite reduction
items.statement: The proof works whenever the type-preserving form torsor reduces to a finite F-subgroup of degree prime to p with the integral finite-etale/spreading control needed by the proof.
items.note: Keep the finite-subgroup reduction as actual supplied data; avoid asserting every reductive form admits a prime-to-p reduction.

items.name: Type G2 residue-characteristic refinement
items.statement: For type G2 the main divisorial local-global conclusion holds if the residue characteristic is not 2, using a finite structure reduction of 2-primary degree.
items.note: Source assertion: p=3 is allowed in this refinement although 3 divides the root-system automorphism order. The finite reduction requires its own prerequisite proof.

items.name: Smoothness in the definition of a parabolic
items.statement: For reductive G/F, an algebraic subgroup P is parabolic when P is smooth and G/P is projective. Projectivity of the quotient alone is insufficient in positive characteristic.
items.note: API: Parabolic predicate, quotient representability and extension of scalars. Tests: (1) G itself is an allowed parabolic; (2) A Borel of split G is parabolic; (3) Do not accept a non-smooth Wenzel subgroup solely from projective quotient.

items.name: A parabolic quotient is transitively acted on over every extension
items.statement: If P⊂G is parabolic, then for every field extension E/F the action G(E) on (G/P)(E) is transitive.
items.note: Borel–Tits conjugacy for rational parabolics; this is stronger than geometric transitivity.

items.name: Universal field-point transitivity gives a rational section
items.statement: For an algebraic subgroup P with projective quotient G/P, if G(E) acts transitively on (G/P)(E) for every E/F, then G→G/P has a rational section.
items.note: Apply the condition to E=F(G/P) and the generic point, using the base coset as the other point.

items.name: A rational section forces smooth connected stabilizer
items.statement: For reductive G/F and P with projective quotient, a rational section of G→G/P implies P is smooth connected.
items.note: After algebraic closure set Q=(P_red)^0; Q is smooth and parabolic, G/Q→G/P is finite with a rational section, hence finite birational onto the normal target and is an isomorphism.

items.name: Smooth stabilizer is exactly parabolic in a projective quotient
items.statement: For P⊂G with G/P projective, P smooth connected implies P smooth, and P smooth implies P parabolic. These complete the five-way equivalence of Proposition 6.1.
items.note: Separate the substantive smoothness implication above from these definition-level implications.

items.name: Twisted flags are universally transitive
items.statement: A twisted flag X of G has transitive G(E)-action on X(E) for every extension E/F.
items.note: Transitivity on an empty X(E) is interpreted as the pairwise property; it does not assert an E-point.

items.name: Universal transitivity characterizes twisted flags
items.statement: Let X be a nonempty integral smooth projective G-variety. If G(E) acts transitively on X(E) for every extension E/F, then X is a twisted flag of G.
items.note: Over F_s choose a smooth point, identify the orbit quotient by its stabilizer, then apply Proposition 6.1. Retain the standing variety convention to exclude the empty scheme.

items.name: Orbit-stabilizer scheme identification
items.statement: Under the universal transitivity hypothesis over a separably closed field and a chosen rational point, the orbit map identifies G/P with the smooth projective variety, with P the scheme-theoretic stabilizer.
items.note: Pointwise geometric transitivity alone cannot erase infinitesimal stabilizer information.

items.name: Finite birational morphism to a normal target is an isomorphism
items.statement: A finite birational morphism from an integral scheme to a normal integral scheme is an isomorphism; apply to G/Q→G/P after the rational section supplies equality of function fields.
items.note: Include finiteness and normality; a general proper birational map need not be an isomorphism.

items.name: Vector groups are R-trivial and additive torsors vanish on affines
items.statement: Affine-space points are directly R-equivalent by linear interpolation, and H1 of a quasi-coherent additive sheaf on an affine scheme is zero; together these justify the vector-torsor step in Lemma 2.3.

items.name: Etale maps remain etale after finite locally free restriction
items.statement: Whenever the relevant Weil restrictions are representable, restriction along a finite locally free base map preserves etale morphisms, including a finite inseparable field extension.

items.name: Etale charts are local analytic isomorphisms over the complete valued field
items.statement: At a rational point of an etale morphism of smooth finite-type F0-schemes, the induced map on F0-points admits a local analytic inverse.
items.note: Bridge the scheme etale Jacobian criterion to the normed analytic inverse function theorem; no finite residue assumption.

items.name: Smooth points lift from the residue field of a henselian local ring
items.statement: For henselian local A and smooth finitely presented X/A, X(A)→X(k) is surjective.
items.note: This geometric statement is beyond a bare ring Hensel predicate; the complete local ring used in Proposition 5.2 supplies the hypothesis.

items.name: Central isogenies and adjoint quotients preserve parabolic schemes
items.statement: The parabolic schemes, types and associated twisted flags of a reductive group are identified with those of its adjoint quotient and of the simply connected cover of its derived group.
items.note: Transport group actions through the central morphisms without claiming surjectivity on all rational group points.

items.name: A power subgroup of torus points is R-trivial
items.statement: For a torus T over a field, a suitable positive integer n has T(L)^n⊂RT(L) for the relevant extensions, via a quasi-trivial torus resolution and an isogeny lifting the power map.
items.note: The exponent is essential. This does not assert T(L)=RT(L). The approximation application remains part of G2.

items.name: Elementary points are dense under the patch-field embedding
items.statement: In the strictly isotropic setting, polynomial coordinates on the unipotent radicals and density F1⊂F0 make G(F1)^+ dense in G(F0)^+ in the comparison needed for Proposition 3.6.
items.note: Prove this for finite products of root/unipotent words and their closures; density of the full G(F1) alone does not imply density of an arbitrary subgroup.

items.name: Finite algebras are Artinian with nilpotent nilradical
items.statement: A module-finite algebra over an Artinian ring is an Artinian ring; the nilradical of a commutative Artinian ring is nilpotent.
items.note: Read Artinian/Module.lean:403 and Artinian/Ring.lean:63. Use these existing results for the finite-algebra tower, not a new Artinian theory.

items.name: Artinian quotient decomposition
items.statement: For commutative Artinian R and n, R/(nilradical R)^n is canonically isomorphic as an R-algebra to the product over maximal ideals m of R/m^n.
items.note: Read Artinian/Module.lean:625. Together with nilradical nilpotence this supplies the product algebra; the finite-local-algebra item only asks for the residue-factor and torsor comparison packaging.

prerequisites.citation: Harbater–Hartmann, Patching over fields (2010), especially Theorem 5.9
prerequisites.why: Full field-intersection, finite model map and tensor-product patch decomposition must be extracted. Their use is read in GP26; the prerequisite paper was not read completely here.

prerequisites.citation: Harbater–Hartmann–Krashen, Local-global principles for torsors over arithmetic curves (2015), Proposition 5.8
prerequisites.why: Completed generic-point to open-patch spreading and analytic-factorization antecedents; retain completed rings and exact local fields.

prerequisites.citation: Harbater–Hartmann–Karemaker–Pop, A comparison between obstructions to local-global principles over semiglobal fields (2020), Theorem 2.5
prerequisites.why: Model comparison needed for the all-rank-one theorem. Exact theorem-level extraction remains required; do not replace rank-one by discrete.

prerequisites.citation: Gille–Stavrova, R-equivalence on group schemes, §2 and Proposition 7.7
prerequisites.why: Ring-valued R-equivalence and henselian elementary-quotient invariance. Proposition 7.7 read directly; the simply connected specialization avoids its more general smooth-cover obstruction.

prerequisites.citation: Petrov–Stavrova, Elementary subgroups of isotropic reductive groups (2008/2009), Theorem 1
prerequisites.why: Independence and normality over semilocal rings, with the strictly proper condition. Full proof extraction remains.

prerequisites.citation: Gille, Le problème de Kneser–Tits, Bourbaki 983 (2009), Theorem 7.2
prerequisites.why: H(k)^+=RH(k) for simply connected strictly isotropic groups. This is not unconditional vanishing of the Whitehead group.

prerequisites.citation: Gille–Parimala–Suresh, Local triviality for G-torsors (2021), Lemmas 3.1 and 3.3
prerequisites.why: Directly read pp. 5–7 for U_last and Lie spanning. Do not import its separate Theorem 7.2 residue-imperfection argument without the May 2026 errata; that theorem is not required by the Lie-span input.

prerequisites.citation: Chernousov–Gille–Reichstein, Reduction of structure for torsors over semilocal rings (2008)
prerequisites.why: Directly read author Theorem 1.2(b) and §§4–5. Own finite integral normalizer reduction and the degree-prime control, including the square-torsion enlargement; reconcile published numbering cited by GP26.

prerequisites.citation: Gille, Loop group schemes and Abhyankar’s lemma (2024), Lemma 3 and Theorems 4,6
prerequisites.why: Published pp. 159–165 read directly. Supply loop-cocycle arithmetic/geometric decomposition, prime-to-p finite-group reduction, smooth proper fixed loci and parabolic descent. Use full local coordinate parameters or explicitly enlarge the divisor.

Add the tame local SNC Kummer-cover theorem as a source-scoped foundation of tame fundamental groups. This is Abhyankar’s local lemma, not the Abhyankar inverse-Galois conjecture or complex Riemann existence.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: semiglobal flags and R-equivalence
routes.brief:
Build Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: semiglobal flags and R-equivalence. Import Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups), especially Layers 2–9, instead of re-planning its group, root, parabolic, central-cover and Chevalley constructions. Import affine Weil restriction and generalized valued-point charts from Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0a, RG2.0), geometry/descent/lifting from Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0–SF.4), and tame covers from Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0–IG.1). Keep these producers independent of this consumer. Existing Mathlib strict submersion and analytic differentiation supply the Banach analysis; do not rebuild them or assume finite dimension over K.

Construct the type-preserving form torsors and smooth projective twisted flags; semilocal R-equivalence and elementary subgroups with nilpotent-Artin invariance; the product-compatible last unipotent subgroup and its Lie spanning chart; corrected analytic factorization on saturated complete T-modules V,W; restriction of projective flags along arbitrary finite, possibly inseparable, extensions. Prove Theorem 3.13 for the specified diamond with F1 dense in F0 and F1 intersect F2=F, using the supplied module hypotheses. Give separate elementary and R-factorization statements with each isotropy hypothesis retained. Optional Proposition 3.11 is quarantined by G2 and must not enter the main dependency chain.

Build the normal-model point/open/branch fields and finite patching system, including the finite P1-model map and tensor decompositions. Prove Z(F) nonempty iff all finite-patch points exist for every reductive G/F and twisted flag Z, and deduce the all-special-fibre-points and unconditional all-rank-one-valuations forms. With a reductive model, prove the discrete-valuations form without a residue-characteristic restriction. State the Tits-index corollaries using Delta_0 equal to minimal-parabolic type: the global subset is the smallest Gamma_F-stable subset containing the transported local subsets. This is an explicitly justified correction, pending G3’s final-version comparison.

For the final theorem let T be any complete DVR, K its fraction field, k its arbitrary residue field, F=K(X) for a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, and p the characteristic exponent of k. If p does not divide the order of the automorphism group of the absolute root system of G_ad, prove Z(F) nonempty iff Z has points over all divisorial completions of F arising from normal projective T-models. It suffices to test those nontrivial on K. Prove the finite-subgroup reduction, SNC spreading, prime-to-p finite-etale loop reduction and loop-parabolic criterion; complete the local ring at P before applying henselian arguments and prove the Grothendieck-completion comparison. The G2 refinement requires residue characteristic different from 2 and its special finite-reduction proof. Do not replace the divisorial family by a fixed model or omit the order hypothesis.

Every definition/construction has an API and three tests in the items. Mandatory boundary tests include nonreduced E tensor F_i, a proper but not strictly proper parabolic in a product, a non-smooth projective quotient in characteristic p, the factorial-pole series outside Frac(k[x][[t]]), and the corrected V/W derivative condition. The tests of finite algebra and Tits-index conventions must import the existing carriers. Prove, rather than encode as structure fields, every external theorem contract. Before implementation, extract the exact prerequisite proof interiors listed in the ledger. Suggested future files may separate REquivalence, AnalyticFactorization, PatchFields and TwistedFlags; this paper job supplies no Lean file and asserts no formalization.
routes.reason: The parent owns algebraic groups and general relative structure, while the existing RG2 continuation concerns local fields with finite residue field, buildings and parahorics. Neither owns semilocal R-equivalence, semiglobal patching or tame-loop flag descent. FunctionFieldArithmetic concerns global finite-constant-field arithmetic and is not this owner. One additional continuation supplies these reusable interfaces without duplicating the existing finite-local-field or number-field Brauer–Manin projects.
